dataset_family: AXIS Neurociencias cohort, Bahia Blanca, Argentina (ViewMind): 65 MCI + 42 controls, native Spanish speakers, followed annually 2017-2020 (40 months). Registry stub P-1026 is the same paper and is excluded.
method_family: Task-based eye tracking (visual short-term memory binding task; fixation duration and saccade amplitude on a GazePoint 150 Hz tracker with chin rest). Group-level linear models, ROC on subject-level summaries among MCI subgroups, and a prospective rule-based conversion prediction.
what_it_shows: Parra, Granada and Fernandez 2022, Alzheimer's & Dementia: DADM. At group level, MCI showed shorter fixation durations and larger saccade amplitudes than age-matched controls (73 vs 72 y) during the VSTMB task. ROC analysis on subject-level summaries separated MCI converters to ADS from stable MCI (AUC 0.95) and MCI-to-other-pathology from stable MCI (AUC 0.60). No AUC is reported for MCI vs controls. A prediction model applied to baseline data classified 36 MCI as likely ADS progressors, and 34 of them (94%) met criteria by year 3. It is single-site with no external validation, and two of the three authors are ViewMind executives.
why: PDF identity confirmed: title, authors (Parra, Granada, Fernandez) and DOI 10.1002/dad2.12386 match the block. I read the whole extract through the references. STATED FORM, partly: its own data support eye-movement behaviour as a biomarker direction for early cognitive decline. MCI differed from controls, and the same measures separated later ADS converters within MCI. 'Scalable' is only asserted ('affordable and non-invasive', 'can support clinical practice in underserved countries', p.7) and never tested. Recording used a research tracker with a chin rest in a 1.5 h session. Scored as round 20 scored P-966. NARROWED FORM, yes: the headline is 'preliminary, single-centre associations with MCI'. The study's own Group (Controls vs MCI) model shows fixation duration and saccade amplitude differing between MCI and controls at group level (Table 1, p.4). Neither channel is externally validated, which matches the wording. Admitting it would widen the eye-movement clause from 'one Korean cohort' with saccadic inhibition/prosaccade latency to a second cohort (Argentina) with memory-task fixation and saccade measures. CAVEATS FOUND IN THE PDF: (1) The inferential statistics look pseudo-replicated. Table 1 reports SE 0.00 and t = -42.11 for a 107-person comparison, which implies fixation-level observations with no stated subject random effect. The group mean differences are large (about 0.33 log units in fixation duration), but their stated significance is overstated. (2) No ROC or AUC for MCI vs controls. The ROC is among MCI subgroups defined by later clinical decisions, is apparently in-sample, and the subgroup sizes are not given in the text. (3) The prediction model is described only as 'based on well-defined eye movement patterns' and is not fully specified. (4) Conversion was adjudicated clinically without AD biomarkers (p.8). (5) Conflict of interest: Parra is ViewMind's Chief Neuroscientific Officer and Fernandez its Chief Scientific Officer (p.10). (6) Single site. The finder who said the block's 'AUC values not stated' is wrong is correct: the PDF gives AUC 0.95/0.60/1.0 (p.7). Independence: Argentina (AXIS Neurociencias). It shares no cohort, site or authors with P-966 (GARD Korea), P-5, P-952 or the other candidates. The narrative review P-105 cites this paper in its Table 1 (p.10, 'Parra et al. 2022 [109]'). P-105 is scored 'no' and adds nothing, so this is not a sample overlap. Not a preprint: peer-reviewed DADM article.

quotes.quote: The study was carried out at AXIS Neurociencias (Bahía Blanca, Buenos Aires, Argentina) and included native Spanish speakers.
A total of 65 MCI patients (mean age of 73 SD 6.1 years, mean years of education = 12) and 42 controls (mean age of 72 SD 6.7 years, mean years of education = 12) were enrolled in the study.
Head movements were minimized using a chin rest. Eye movements (i.e., fixation duration and saccade amplitude) were recorded with a GazePoint eye tracker, with a sampling rate of 150 Hz.
Control vs MCI X BC -0.33 0.00 -42.11 ... Control vs. MCI X BC 1.09 0.05 18.93 ... Threshold of significance is set at t = ±1.95.
the log mean fixation duration was significantly shorter in MCI than in Controls, when considering the encoding phase of the BC condition (t = –42.11 and t = –37.72, BC and UC, respectively).
When considering saccade amplitudes, MCI had longer saccades than Controls while encoding BC and UC, with the difference more pronounced in the BC condition (t = 18.93 and t = 14.90, respectively).

we used aggregate subject-based summaries of eye movement measures to predict group membership using ROC analysis. This analysis aimed to determine whether oculomotor behaviors were able to differentiate MCI_C from MCI and from MCI_O. The analysis revealed that our eye-tracking metrics achieved 95% sensitivity and 95% specificity to distinguish between MCI and MCI_C patients (area under the curve [AUC] = 0.95). When distinguishing between MCI and MCI_O, the sensitivity was 60% and the specificity was about 75% (AUC = 0.60).

The model predicted that of the 65 MCI patients, 36 would likely progress to ADS, whereas the rest would not progress to this form of dementia. ... at year 3, 34 of the 36 identified as potential ADS converters (94%) met diagnostic criteria.
as we did not have access to the biomarkers for AD recently recommended,26 we adhered to the recommendations of the consensus group and used the term ADS based on clinical decisions.
